evidence: bp-node.lisp:415-419: on-ready drives `(list :session peer session-id t mru obs ...)` (session open). The normal path closes it at 443-446 `(list :session peer session-id nil 1 ...)`, but the handler at 450-451 `((not sent) (fnn-out "BP forwarding session unavailable: ~a" e))` returns without driving the close. Only the `t` branch (468-471) drives it.
fix: Whenever the on-ready open was driven, drive the `:session ... nil` close event in the handler (and in an unwind-protect), regardless of `sent`.

reviewer: bp-node.lisp:415-419: on-ready drives (:session peer session-id t ...) once the session is established. The close (:session ... nil 1) is driven only on the normal path (443-446) or in the handler's t branch (465-471). The (not sent) branch (450-451) only prints. A peer reset after SESS_INIT, when the open issued no send, leaves the session in the machine. fn-bpnrd-serve-rotation-due-p (books/bp-node-rotation-due.lisp:233-241) requires (null (fn-bpnp-sessions st)), so serve rotation is blocked until restart and the journal keeps growing. Reaching this needs the hop to reset during a forward session with nothing to send.
scenario: The hop completes SESS_INIT (the ACL2 :session open is driven) and the open answers no cl-send, or the peer resets before the effect fires. fnn-recv then raises ECONNRESET. The machine keeps session-id open. Serve rotation requires "no outbound session" at a safe point (comment at 588-589), so a stale open session can block fn-bpnrd-serve-rotation-due-p, and the per-peer session state is left inconsistent until restart.
title: Forward session: a connection error before the attempt is issued skips the ACL2 session-close event
